description: Incremental Phase 3 evidence for the 0.8.0 roadmap close-out: Phase 3A adds Context Menu, Phase 3B adds Data Table. Passing backfill evidence does not add a component to the package manifest's certifiedComponents list until the 0.8.0 release gate is complete.

resolvedFindings: Bootstrap Dropdown's documented `reference` option (an object providing getBoundingClientRect, i.e. a Popper virtual element) cleanly supports pointer-coordinate placement; no separate Moo-owned positioning layer was needed. Moo owns only contextmenu/Shift+F10/ContextMenu-key invocation, the virtual-reference bridge, the explicit fallback trigger, focus-into-menu-on-open, and Escape focus return to the invoking trigger.

The fallback trigger keeps `data-bs-toggle="dropdown"` as the sibling Bootstrap's own menu lookup and Up/Down/Escape-in-menu keydown delegation resolve against, so arrow-key roving focus and outside-click dismissal stay inherited from Bootstrap Dropdown rather than reimplemented.
limitations: Phase 3A browser automation currently covers the canonical Bootstrap 5.3.3 lane in Chromium; a later gate will rerun the supported Bootstrap and browser matrices.

The fixture proves explicit public ESM initialization, getInstance/getOrCreateInstance/dispose lifecycle, pointer right-click open at pointer coordinates, Shift+F10 and ContextMenu-key keyboard open anchored to the trigger, the explicit fallback trigger for touch/keyboard-only use, focus entry into the menu, Escape dismissal with focus return to the invoking trigger, outside-click dismissal, enabled item activation, disabled item non-activation and focus skip, viewport-edge collision clamping, responsive/RTL/theme rendering, accessibility, and clean console/page-error evidence.
Nested submenus are out of scope for Phase 3A; the component page documents this as an explicit known gap rather than approximating hover/roving submenu behavior it cannot back.
The normalized screenshot is a render smoke and has no accepted regression baseline yet.
Real-device and generic host-conformance evidence remain pending.

resolvedFindings: Bootstrap ships no table JS plugin at all (verified: no js/src/table.js in the vendored or reference source), so sorting, free-text search, faceted multi-select filtering, column visibility, row selection, and client-side pagination are entirely Moo-owned, operating on a fully server-rendered table (every row exists in the DOM at load; the runtime only reorders, hides, or paginates existing rows).

The per-column sort menu and the toolbar's faceted filter/view-options menus reuse Bootstrap's own Dropdown Data API and dropdown-item markup; only the sort/filter/visibility state machine and the facet checkbox indicator (a persistent square with no Bootstrap dropdown-item equivalent) are Moo-owned.
limitations: Phase 3B browser automation currently covers the canonical Bootstrap 5.3.3 lane in Chromium; a later gate will rerun the supported Bootstrap and browser matrices.

The fixture proves explicit public ESM initialization, getInstance/getOrCreateInstance/dispose lifecycle, text search, faceted Status/Priority filtering, single-column Asc/Desc/Hide sorting, column visibility toggling kept in sync between the column header and the View menu, row selection with an indeterminate select-all state, pagination composed with the active filter/sort state, responsive/RTL/theme rendering, accessibility, and clean console/page-error evidence.
No remote data engine: the component operates on a fixed, fully server-rendered dataset, matching the Phase 3B non-goal.
The normalized screenshot is a render smoke and has no accepted regression baseline yet.
Real-device and generic host-conformance evidence remain pending.
